A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Transformers Struggle to Learn to Search. Their text, equations, figures, algorithm, and appendices are readable. v2 retains the earlier material and adds Appendix A.12, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer experiments on graph search, natural-language proof search, scaling, DFS, and selection-inference, plus mechanistic analyses and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds layer-wise path-merge distributions investigating search direction in Appendix A.12 and Figures 18–19.

M1.justification: The transformer architectures, training objectives, input representations, and reconstruction procedure in Section 4.1 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Appendix A.12 applies the existing interpretability method without modifying it.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same graph distributions and symbolic search, natural-language proof search, DFS, and selection-inference tasks. Appendix A.12 examines lookahead-9 graphs within existing coverage, without adding a distinct task or input scenario.

E2.justification: The model comparisons in Figures 2 and 5, including Figure 5's untrained control, are retained. Appendix A.12 analyzes two previously evaluated balanced-distribution models and introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.12 adds an analysis protocol using 100 lookahead-9 examples for models trained with maximum lookaheads 20 and 12. It restricts path-merge counts to the start-to-goal path and reports source-target frequencies by layer. Existing experimental protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 Section 4.2 allows either forward or backward search without directly investigating direction. v2 adds a focused mechanistic analysis of this question through Appendix A.12 and Figures 18–19, extending the existing analysis in a limited way.

E5.justification: Existing seed counts and minimum-over-seeds reporting remain unchanged, including the 14-seed scaling experiments and five-seed natural-language experiments. The added heatmaps introduce no uncertainty estimates or controlled repeated-seed analysis; seed dependence is only suggested as an interpretation.

E6.justification: Figures 18–19 add path-merge distributions. For the maximum-lookahead-20 model, A.12 reports predominant copying from positions i-1, i-1, i-2, and i-4 across layers 1–4; the maximum-lookahead-12 model exhibits mixed directional patterns. Existing results in Figures 1–17 are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–10, reconstruction algorithm, and reasoning about exponential path merging are unchanged. Appendix A.12 contributes empirical observations without adding or revising formal assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The principal claims about learning search from suitable data, exponential path merging, and difficulties with graph size, model scaling, and intermediate steps remain unchanged. The abstract's explicit emphasis on parallel search restates a claim already present in v1's introduction and Section 4.2.

C2.justification: Appendix A.12 interprets the new patterns as backward search in one model and mixed directions in another. It suggests initialization-dependent direction and explicitly calls for further experiments, adding a qualified interpretation to v1's statement that either direction is possible.

D1.justification: Figures 18–19 specify the path restriction and per-target normalization used to construct the new heatmaps. Figure 2's caption now explicitly states a maximum graph size of 41 vertices, while Section 3.1.1 retains the 128-token input setting. These are limited documentation additions; code access and existing implementation details are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and research positioning are unchanged. Bibliographic content matches across versions; reference reflow and the added acknowledgment do not change positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes a short abstract revision, adds Appendix A.12, expands the acknowledgments, and adds conference-publication headers. The main narrative, section order, and existing appendix organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 18–19, each containing six layer-specific heatmaps with source-target axes and a frequency color scale. It revises Figure 2's caption and makes limited header and layout changes. Existing figures retain their content, with some plot panels rasterized.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.12 and Figures 18–19 give useful empirical detail to v1's unresolved discussion of search direction while preserving the existing evidence. The gain is limited: initialization dependence is not isolated because the two models also differ in training lookahead, and v2 acknowledges that further experiments are needed. Overall, the revision modestly improves the mechanistic account.
